sections.title: Greetings and a last session
sections.summary: They sort out which app to use for calls, agree to record audio only, and the student says this will be their last conversation for now because of a heavier schedule.

sections.title: The tutor's feedback tool
sections.summary: The tutor shows a webpage that analyzes the student's recorded speech, and they discuss how useful it would be for learners and in Taiwan.

sections.title: Exams and Chinese writing
sections.summary: The student explains that their exams are in January and July and that they find Chinese writing hard, even though they got good scores last year.

sections.title: A difficult essay prompt
sections.summary: The tutor reads an essay prompt about the distance between people, and they discuss how to approach it with creative storytelling and how the student improved.

sections.title: Chinese writing exam and cram schools
sections.summary: The student explains that the difficulty is organizing a story that appeals to examiners, and why they avoid cram schools.

sections.title: Subjectivity and bias in grading
sections.summary: The tutor describes how bias from cram schools and graders makes writing scores hard to predict.

sections.title: Luck, expectations and resilience
sections.summary: The student talks about getting a lucky A, and they discuss Olympic medals, high school, and disliking exam writing.

sections.title: What is the real English?
sections.summary: The tutor and student discuss the origins of English, accents, and whether any one version is the real one.

sections.title: India, English and accents
sections.summary: The speakers discuss India's growing influence on English, how different Englishes can be hard to understand, and how people define "correct" English.

sections.title: Speaking English in Taiwan
sections.summary: The student explains that speaking English with bilingual friends in Taiwan can make people think you are not local enough, and the tutor links this to nationalism and conformity in other countries.

sections.title: Memes and The Selfish Gene
sections.summary: The tutor recommends The Selfish Gene and explains that a meme is anything passed from one person to another non-genetically, including ideology and culture.

sections.title: Sleepless thinking, AI and doubt
sections.summary: The tutor describes times when big questions or AI kept him awake, and the conversation moves to being trapped in time and the value of doubt.

sections.title: Religion vs. organized religion
sections.summary: The tutor distinguishes religion from organized religion and says doubt is essential, while the tutor's own Christian upbringing is used as an example.

sections.title: Growing up Christian in Taiwan
sections.summary: The student describes six generations of Christians in the family, a childhood with no choice about faith, and the tutor compares it to being told to attend cram school.

sections.title: Theology, polytheism and atheists
sections.summary: They discuss mathematical proof, monotheism versus polytheism, and the idea that Christians and atheists differ by only one god.

sections.title: The Allegory of the Cave, new words and practicing English
sections.summary: The student retells the cave allegory, the tutor adds the words shackle and yoke, and the talk turns to doubt, the status quo and practicing English in Taiwan.

sections.title: Accents and where Chinese was learned
sections.summary: The tutor explains how his Chinese was shaped by mainland influences and how people hear his accent differently.

sections.title: Looking like a local everywhere
sections.summary: The tutor describes being mistaken for a local in many countries and the one time he was called an American.

sections.title: Practicing English and pricing lessons
sections.summary: They discuss whether Taiwanese people want to practice English and how the tutor's lesson prices affected interest.

sections.title: Why foreigners get paid more
sections.summary: The student asks whether foreigners deserve higher wages, and they discuss visas, government rules, supply and demand, and history.

sections.title: Pay gaps for foreign and local teachers
sections.summary: The speakers discuss how foreign teachers are paid more than local teachers in cram schools and why local teachers may feel upset.

sections.title: Cram school costs and raising children
sections.summary: They compare how much cram school costs from elementary school through high school and how expensive it is to raise a child in Taiwan.

sections.title: Teacher workload, free markets and salary negotiation
sections.summary: They return to how local and foreign teachers are paid, then talk about low salaries in Taiwan and negotiating job offers in America.

sections.title: Ambition, faith and Darwin
sections.summary: They discuss whether American culture is losing ambition, then whether scientists can be religious, and Darwin's plant experiments.

sections.title: Great thinkers and their era
sections.summary: The student discusses Darwin and Da Vinci and argues that they were considered geniuses mainly because of the time they lived in.

sections.title: Science, faith and the watch argument
sections.summary: The tutor and student discuss religion, scientists and faith, and the student questions Newton's watch argument for a designer.

sections.title: AI, The Matrix and living in a simulation
sections.summary: They discuss whether life could be a simulation, and the student agrees, citing physics and the expanding universe.

sections.title: Rick and Morty, caring about life and 'introspective'
sections.summary: The student uses Rick from Rick and Morty to argue that we should keep caring even if life is fake, and they clear up the words 'sensitive' and 'introspective'.

sections.title: Purpose, paradox and life
sections.summary: The tutor explains that he doesn't think life needs a purpose and that his actions can be paradoxical, and the student connects this to the show Rick.

sections.title: Ego, embarrassment and discomfort
sections.summary: The tutor explains the premise of his podcast: letting go of ego and not letting embarrassment or discomfort rule your choices.

sections.title: Literal or metaphorical podcast title
sections.summary: The student asks whether the podcast title is literal or a metaphor, and the tutor shares stories and explains what success means for the project.

sections.title: Student's shyness and wrap-up
sections.summary: The student describes how shyness shaped his childhood and school life, then both discuss future talks, attention and his exam timing.

sections.title: Being curious
sections.summary: The student describes himself as a curious person and explains how his past experience gave him a 'spider sense' for people starting businesses.

sections.title: Entrepreneurs, karma and real value
sections.summary: The student explains why he loves talking to entrepreneurs, how helping friends has come back to him, and why he distrusts businesses and real estate that create no real value.

sections.title: Vocabulary and language experiences
sections.summary: The student talks about his limited vocabulary and confidence, and the group shares experiences of forgetting and relearning languages.

sections.title: Scheduling and exams
sections.summary: They discuss how often to meet around the January and July college exams, and why switching between activities takes so much energy.

sections.title: Meeting once a month
sections.summary: The student suggests meeting monthly, and the tutor explains why a less regular schedule is harder to arrange.

sections.title: The student's free time
sections.summary: The student describes how little he leaves home now that he is no longer diving.

sections.title: Scheduling the next session

patterns.title: Missing articles before singular countable nouns
patterns.tip: Singular countable nouns, including grades, usually need 'a', 'an' or 'the'. Check words like 'B', 'guess', 'metaphor' and 'sermon' before you say them.

patterns.title: Keeping past-tense stories in the past
patterns.tip: When you tell a story about the past, keep every verb in the past tense, including those in 'when' and 'if' clauses. Don't slip back into the present halfway through.

patterns.title: Subject-verb agreement
patterns.tip: Match the verb to the real subject. Add -s for he/she/it in the present, and use 'are/were' with plural subjects. Uncountable nouns like 'value' take singular verbs.

patterns.title: Singular and plural noun forms
patterns.tip: Decide whether the noun is countable or uncountable, then match it to words like 'those', 'different', 'two' and 'many'. 'Land' and 'real estate' stay singular, while 'sizes', 'times' and 'geniuses' need the plural.

patterns.title: Using a noun where a verb is needed
patterns.tip: Check that the word you use is a verb when the sentence needs an action. Many words have a separate verb form, such as 'narrate', 'originate' and 'succeed'.

patterns.title: Prepositions and collocations
patterns.tip: Many verbs and adjectives take a specific preposition, so learn them as a set: 'suck at', 'in junior high', 'talk to', 'communicate with', 'tell someone about'.
